purpose: Evidence packet for agentic-product-development, coding-agents-full-stack and agentic-evals-swe-bench-trajectories; atomic claims, primary-source locators, contradictory updates and limits.

sources.title: SWE-bench official leaderboards
sources.read_scope: full page definition, news, benchmark links; leaderboard dynamic rows not independently executed
claim_locators: Lines 49–81: resolved definition, 2294 original instances, 500 Verified instances, Bash Only mini-SWE-agent view
Lines 101–104: newer ProgramBench and CodeClash benchmarks
limitations: Results depend on task split and agent environment. This ledger records benchmark definition, not a live model ranking.

sources.title: Introducing SWE-bench Verified
sources.read_scope: task annotation and dataset construction sections
claim_locators: Dataset construction, lines 160–190
limitations: Human filtering improves task feasibility but does not prove complete test coverage or absence of later training contamination.

sources.title: Why SWE-bench Verified no longer measures frontier coding capabilities
sources.read_scope: background, test-design audit, contamination method and examples, discussion
claim_locators: Summary lines 40–49; selected audit lines 68–74; contamination method lines 267–284
limitations: 138 audited tasks were selected from problems o3 did not consistently solve; 59.4% is not a random-sample estimate for all 500 tasks. Audit is OpenAI-reported; contamination examples do not establish every model/task is contaminated.

sources.title: Separating signal from noise in coding evaluations
sources.read_scope: full substantive article excluding unrelated navigation and code-example formatting
claim_locators: Lines 35–50: 731 public tasks and estimated ~30% broken
Lines 51–64: pipeline and five-engineer reviews
Lines 70–75: retracts Pro recommendation
limitations: Publisher is a model provider. Automated screening plus review of flagged tasks can miss flaws outside the flagged subset; the ~30% number is an audit estimate, not a universal property of coding tasks.

sources.title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
sources.read_scope: abstract, background, methodology, results, key caveats and overgeneralization appendix
claim_locators: Abstract; §2 Methodology; §3 Results; §4.1 Key Caveats; Appendix B overgeneralizations
Official companion https://metr.org/blog/2025-07-10-early-2025-ai-experienced-os-dev-study/ lines 46–63
limitations: 16 developers with established repository expertise; 246 tasks in mature open-source projects; primarily Cursor with early-2025 Claude models. Total implementation time was self-reported, including review. Does not estimate all developers or October 2026 tools.

sources.title: We are Changing our Developer Productivity Experiment Design
claim_locators: Lines 35–64: raw estimates, selection and concurrent-agent time issues; lines 70–80: redesigned research options
limitations: Selection of developers and tasks, changed pay, incomplete AI-disallowed tasks and concurrent work compromise current causal interpretation. Both later-study confidence intervals include zero.

sources.title: Measuring the Self-Reported Impact of Early-2026 AI on Technical Worker Productivity
sources.read_scope: summary, sampling/methodology, detailed value-speed distinction and caveats
claim_locators: Summary lines 35–52; value/speed discussion and convenience sampling lines 82–93
limitations: Self-reported counterfactuals; convenience sample; low approximately 2% emailed response rate; nonrepresentative recruitment. Internal consistency does not verify real causal productivity gains.

sources.title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
sources.read_scope: full maintainer project page, benchmark setting and Google Drive exclusion notice
claim_locators: Lines 9–20: real desktop tasks and execution-based setup/evaluation; lines 64–79: 369 vs 361 permitted task counts
limitations: Network-dependent tasks and maximum action budget can alter comparability. Original 2024 baseline results describe historical models, not current capability.

sources.title: GAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants
sources.read_scope: abstract, question design, answer evaluation, task composition and limitations
claim_locators: §3.2 lines 139–140: quasi-exact answer scoring
§3.3 lines 143–147: 466 questions and action limitations
§6 Limitations
limitations: Question-answer evaluation does not measure write actions such as posting, uploads or booking. Web facts can change. Language/cultural diversity and human annotation costs limit coverage.

sources.title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
sources.read_scope: abstract, environment construction, reward metric, empirical results, failure analyses; appendix conversations treated as examples
claim_locators: §3 lines 174–182: final database/output reward and pass^k versus pass@k
§5.1 lines 216–239: trial budgets, historical table and repeated success
License line 44: CC BY 4.0
limitations: Simulated users and simplified retail/airline policies. Matching the final database/output can still miss intermediate policy violations. Original model results are historical.

sources.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
sources.read_scope: abstract, composition, evaluation setup, failure analysis and validity taxonomy
claim_locators: Abstract lines 84–87; composition lines 102–122; Appendix J.1 lines 1701–1733
License line 79: CC BY 4.0
limitations: Eight heterogeneous text-based environments; aggregate score combines different tasks/metrics. Historical 29-model experiment does not rank current tools.

sources.title: OSWorld 2.0: Benchmarking Computer Use Agents on Long-Horizon Real-World Tasks
sources.read_scope: abstract, task construction, challenge phenomena, evaluation release/scoring discipline, limitations
claim_locators: Abstract lines 131–135; §2.2 task construction; Table 2 lines 239–253; §6 limitations lines 407–410
limitations: 108 tasks are diagnostic, not representative of all professions. Scores depend on release, action settings, task mix and stochastic behavior; paper HTML content/abstract-version model details should be reconciled before quoting a live ranking.

sources.title: ProgramBench: Can Language Models Rebuild Programs From Scratch?
sources.read_scope: full definition, harness, security controls, scoring and contamination FAQ; dynamic rankings not imported
claim_locators: Lines 11–20: task and primary metric
Lines 61–68: binary, documentation, code-free environment and 200 tasks
Lines 89–126: harness, resolved metric and contamination discussion
limitations: Complete behavioral equivalence against compiled programs is narrower than open-ended product usefulness. Tests are finite; open-source programs may have been seen in training. Partial test percentage must not be relabeled fully resolved.

claims.public_wording: SWE-bench Verified is a human-filtered 500-task subset of real repository issues; its resolved metric records tasks that pass the benchmark tests.
claims.locator: Official benchmark definitions; 2024 release Dataset construction
limitations: Test success does not establish UI quality, security, maintainability, deployment correctness or product-market fit.

limitations: Selected hard/failing-task sample; retain denominator and selection rule. Attribute the audit to OpenAI.

claims.public_wording: In July 2026, OpenAI estimated that about 30% of the SWE-Bench Pro public tasks had breaking issues and retracted its earlier recommendation to adopt that benchmark.
limitations: Estimate comes from automated screening plus independent review of flagged tasks; vendor-reported audit.

claims.public_wording: METR’s early-2025 randomized study of 16 experienced open-source developers and 246 tasks found that allowing the tested AI tools increased completion time by 19%.
limitations: Dates, participants and setting must remain in public wording. This is not a claim that October 2026 coding agents slow all developers.

claims.public_wording: METR’s February 2026 update judged its later experiment an unreliable signal of current AI productivity effects because of developer/task selection and time-measurement problems.
limitations: Does not reverse the earlier RCT by establishing a reliable current speedup.

claims.public_wording: In the later study, raw estimated time changes were −18% for returning developers (interval −38% to +9%) and −4% for new developers (−15% to +9%); METR warns against treating those estimates as reliable current effects.
limitations: Both intervals include zero. Selection effects and concurrent work compromise interpretation.

claims.public_wording: METR’s February–April 2026 survey of 349 technical workers reported a median self-assessed 1.4–2× change in work value from AI; the authors caution that those perceptions may not match reality.
limitations: Self-reported convenience sample with low response; no causal effect estimate. Speed and value are distinct measures.

claims.public_wording: OSWorld evaluates desktop agents through real applications and execution-based final-state checks; maintainers permit either 369 tasks or 361 after excluding eight network-dependent Google Drive tasks.
claims.locator: Project description and Google Drive Tasks notice
limitations: Report task count, maximum steps and environment; original model baseline numbers are historical.

claims.public_wording: GAIA contains 466 assistant questions scored with a normalized, quasi-exact match to short factual answers. It does not evaluate actions such as posting content or booking a meeting.
limitations: A correct short answer does not certify the trace, write authorization or end-to-end product workflow.
claims.freshness_trigger: benchmark version, evaluation harness, model release, replication, study update, or maintainer correction

claims.public_wording: τ-bench distinguishes pass@k, at least one success in k trials, from pass^k, success in every one of k trials; these answer different reliability questions.
limitations: The trials concern the same underlying simulated task with conversation variation; do not treat repeated-trial success as independent real-world deployment certification.
claims.freshness_trigger: benchmark version, evaluation harness, model release, replication, study update, or maintainer correction

claims.public_wording: The original τ-bench reward checks final database state and required output information, and the paper explicitly notes that a passing episode can still violate a policy such as required user confirmation.
limitations: Requires supplementary trajectory/policy evaluation for intermediate violations.
claims.freshness_trigger: benchmark version, evaluation harness, model release, replication, study update, or maintainer correction

claims.public_wording: AgentBench spans eight text-interactive environments including operating-system, database, knowledge-graph, game, household, shopping and web tasks.
limitations: Heterogeneous environment scores should not be converted into a universal agent reliability percentage.
claims.freshness_trigger: benchmark version, evaluation harness, model release, replication, study update, or maintainer correction

claims.public_wording: AgentBench separates completed episodes, context-limit failures, invalid response formats, invalid actions and task-limit failures.
limitations: This is a diagnostic taxonomy from the benchmark, not an exhaustive product incident taxonomy.

claims.public_wording: OSWorld 2.0 expands computer-use evaluation to 108 end-to-end workflows with challenges such as cross-source reasoning, changing environments, hidden state, conflict resolution and proactive user interaction.
limitations: No claim of occupation-wide representativeness or comparability with OSWorld 1.0 percentages.
claims.freshness_trigger: benchmark version, evaluation harness, model release, replication, study update, or maintainer correction

claims.public_wording: ProgramBench asks agents to rebuild 200 programs from executable behavior and documentation without original source access or internet use; the primary metric is complete resolution against the hidden behavioral tests.
limitations: Average test pass rate and ≥95% almost-resolved are auxiliary metrics. Finite tests cannot certify every possible input.
claims.freshness_trigger: benchmark version, evaluation harness, model release, replication, study update, or maintainer correction

claims.public_wording: A product research program should measure patch correctness, complete artifacts, answer accuracy, desktop state and interaction-policy compliance separately before combining them into a release decision.
claims.locator: Derived from distinct benchmark task definitions
limitations: FrankX architectural recommendation; sources describe different units and do not validate this exact release framework.

claims.public_wording: An agent-product experiment should record accepted useful work, human review time, rework, cost, latency and policy violations; raw tokens or task counts cannot alone establish productivity.
claims.locator: Derived from implementation-time measurement and value/speed distinctions
limitations: Proposed measurement contract; this exact composite has not been empirically validated here.

contrary_evidence_sequence.event: METR narrow early-2025 RCT finds slowdown
OpenAI withdraws Verified reporting and recommends Pro
METR later-study signal is compromised; raw intervals include zero
METR survey shows higher perceived value with explicit self-report/selection caveats
OpenAI retracts Pro recommendation after further audit

do_not_publish: AI coding agents are 19% slower today.
AI doubles technical worker productivity (presenting self-report as causal).
59.4% of all SWE-bench Verified tasks are broken (wrong denominator/selection).
Use SWE-Bench Pro as the clean substitute for Verified (superseded recommendation).
A current model wins because its vendor benchmark percentage exceeds another number obtained with a different harness.
τ-bench final-state success proves every intermediate authorization/policy requirement was followed.
Historical OSWorld/GAIA/AgentBench model baselines represent October 2026 capability.
ProgramBench average behavioral-test pass rate equals fully resolved instance percentage.

measurement_contract.comparison_rule: Use matched or randomized tasks where practicable, retain failed and abandoned runs, separate self-report from observed outcomes, and state selection and coverage limits.
